subject: Post-call recap — HarborBank pilot economics, caching & batching levers
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@harborbank.com>, Tom Everett <tom.everett@harborbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — HarborBank pilot economics, caching & batching levers

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks for a productive 30-minute discovery today. Quick recap while points are fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can align on budget and scope.

Key pain & goals you shared:
- Production fraud scoring pipeline has very high token volume (both request + context). Current spend is the blocker for a wider rollout.
- Need to preserve 95th-pct latency target (~<120ms external-facing) and not degrade model quality (false-positive tolerance is low).
- Procurement wants a predictable TCO for a 3-month pilot and a clear path to a hosted vs private deployment decision.
- Budget constraint: pilot budget ceiling of ~USD 80k / quarter (you mentioned this as a hard gate for Q4 trials).

Initial economics framing (ballpark, post-call):
1) Baseline (hosted, no batching/cache): easiest to ship but highest unit cost. Useful as a short-term comparison baseline.
2) Expected (hosted + caching + smart batching): we expect 35–55% unit-cost reduction for your workload shape by applying KV/prefix caching and continuous batching for short-lived transactions. This keeps latency SLO while lowering per-inference spend.
3) Aggressive (dedicated capacity + int8/4-bit quantization + cache): with a reserved pool and quantized weights we can materially reduce token compute; this is the lowest-cost path but requires procurement lead time for committed capacity and possibly a private deployment for stricter controls.

Open assumptions we used in today's sketch:
- Typical request length ~120 tokens, average session context ~350 tokens, burst qps up to ~200 for peak windows. Please correct if off.
- Quality targets: no measurable uplift in false positives attributable to quantization or beam/pruning changes.

Actionable next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood -> share short SOW (attached v1) + three simple cost scenarios (baseline/expected/aggressive) with line items for tokens, reserved capacity, and pilot engineering hours. (I attached v1; see updates below.)
2) HarborBank -> confirm pilot budget ceiling and procurement timeline (PO windows).
3) Technical -> schedule a 2-hour benchmarking session where you provide a representative sample trace (we requested a 48-hour sample; sample_workload_histogram.csv attached). We'll run a controlled perf test modelling your peak bursts to quantify latency and warm-cache benefits.
4) Pricing -> propose a 3-month pilot with an option for committed token blocks and a one-time setup fee. Karthik will propose concrete pricing options in this thread.

Questions for you before we finalize SOW v2:
- Confirm the hard budget number for the pilot (you mentioned ~80k — is that per quarter or per pilot total?).
- Do you require a private/VPC deployment for the pilot or is hosted acceptable for an initial benchmark?
- Any additional security artifacts needed (SOC2 snippets, encryption-at-rest confirmation)? We can attach the compliance pack.

If this aligns, I’ll update the SOW with the options and send a DocuSign link for quick signoff on the pilot scope.

Thanks again — good alignment on the core trade-offs; I’ll wait for your budget confirmation and preferred dates for the bench run.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: HarborBank_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf; sample_workload_histogram.csv; batching_cache_example.pptx

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@harborbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Everett <tom.everett@harborbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — HarborBank pilot economics, caching & batching levers

Thanks Soojin — this is a helpful recap. A few clarifications from my side:
- The USD 80k number I mentioned is the pilot total for the 3-month window (not per quarter). That is our ceiling unless we get executive signoff.
- Hosted is acceptable for the initial benchmark as long as data-in-transit and rest meet our controls; we will escalate private/VPC if the pilot looks promising.
- Procurement timeline: we typically need a signed SOW + PO 3–4 weeks out. Tom (procurement) is copied and will confirm exact calendar constraints.

I appreciate the three-option framing. Two asks before we sign: 1) make the SOW explicit about what metrics we’ll measure (latency p50/p95, cost per API call, cache hit-rate) and 2) a short line in the SOW saying Redwood will own the bench run execution and provide raw perf logs for our audit.

On the sample: I’ll share a 48-hour trace today via secure upload with masked PII fields.

—Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Fraud Analytics | HarborBank
sara.lim@harborbank.com | +1 617-555-0987

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — HarborBank pilot economics, caching & batching levers

Quick internal note on pricing options we should offer HarborBank:

Option A — No commitment (benchmark-only):
- Hosted pay-as-you-go; higher unit rates but zero contract friction. Good for fast benchmarks and immediate comparison to their current spend.
- Include 2 weeks of complimentary bench run credits (to remove friction).

Option B — Pilot commitment (recommended):
- 3-month pilot, committed token block with a tiered discount: 15% off hosted list for committed volume, plus a one-time pilot setup credit to offset initial engineering hours.
- Add a 30% reserved-capacity uplift option if they want predictable latency during peak windows (reserved pool billed monthly).

Option C — Dedicated reserved (enterprise trial):
- 6–12 week dedicated pool, steeper discount (~30–40% vs payg), but requires procurement lead time and minimal monthly commit. Best if HarborBank wants lowest unit economics post-pilot.

Operational notes:
- For the bench run, ask them to provide representative traces and annotate expected production SLAs. We should instrument for cache-hit-rate and token-distribution to validate our 35–55% savings hypothesis.
- Engineering needs ~48–72 hours to set up a controlled run once we have sample traces.

I’ll draft a simple pricing table to include in SOW v2 — keep it conservative to avoid surprises.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Pricing | Redwood Inference

Sara / Tom —

Thanks for confirming the USD 80k total pilot ceiling — that’s clear and helpful. I updated SOW v1 accordingly and attached SOW_v2 (embedded in the DocuSign link below) that includes:
- Explicit measurement plan (p50/p95 latency, cost per API call, cache hit-rate, false positive delta).
- Redwood will run the bench and provide raw perf logs and a short technical audit report for HarborBank.
- Three pricing scenarios (A/B/C) with the recommended Pilot Commitment option highlighted.

Links / quick items:
- DocuSign SOW v2 (sign + return): https://www.docusign.com/sandbox/embedded-signer-link/ABC123
- Proposed bench run window: Oct 27–29 (we can shift to Nov 3–5 if procurement needs extra lead time). Please confirm preferred slot.
- Deliverables: perf run results, cost comparison table, recommended production deploy path (hosted -> reserved -> private if desired).

Next asks from HarborBank:
1) Confirm bench-run window (Oct 27–29 or Nov 3–5).
2) Share the 48-hour masked trace upload link (Sara said she’d share today).
3) Procurement: if you can share any standard PO terms or procurement templates up front, that will speed contracting.

We’ll hold the recommended pilot pricing in SOW v2 for 10 business days from signature to keep flexibility. Once signed we will schedule the perf run and assign an engineering lead.

If that reads correctly I’ll route the DocuSign now.

Best,
Soojin Lee
